01.n: Gesenius: to bind, to make fast; the brief's lexicon also gives 'imprison'. 'Him' is Jehoahaz, whom the BSB names. The 'and' that begins the verse is part of this word.

02.r: The title of the Egyptian king.
02.n: Gesenius: a common title of the ancient kings of Egypt, sometimes joined to a particular name, and he gives 'Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt' as an example.

03.r: The Egyptian king who now controlled Judah.
03.n: Gesenius: Necho, king of Egypt, son of Psammetichus, called Necho the second to distinguish him from his grandfather.

04.r: The place where Neco held his prisoner.
04.n: Gesenius: a town at the northern border of Palestine, in the land of Hamath.

06.r: A kingdom of Syria to the north of Israel.
06.n: Gesenius: a distinguished city of Syria on the Orontes, on the northern frontier of the Holy Land.

s: so that he could not reign
07.r: Neco removed Jehoahaz from the throne.
07.n: Literally 'from reigning': the preposition 'from' before the verb means 'so as not to'. YLT keeps it. The Geneva reads it as 'while he reigned', a different sense.
t: so that he could not reign

09.r: Neco imposed a payment on Judah.
09.n: The verb 'to give', here in the sense put or set; STEPBible tags this occurrence 'put'. BDB: give, put, set.

10.r: A sum exacted from a defeated land.
10.n: Gesenius: fine, amercement, money exacted from anyone, citing this verse. BDB: indemnity, fine. Our register keeps 'fine' for this word, apart from 'tribute'; the KJV, Geneva and ASV say 'tribute', the BSB 'levy'.

11.r: The fine falls on the land.

14.r: A large unit of weight for precious metal.
14.n: The brief's lexicon: a round weight, talent. The word is singular after the number, as Hebrew counts.

15.n: Our register keeps 'silver' for this word.

_extra.21: ἑκατὸν (a hundred): the Greek has 'a hundred talents of gold', where the Hebrew has one talent.

01.n: Dictionary form supplied; the brief gives none. μετέστησεν, 'he removed', from μεθίστημι: the Greek has Neco remove him rather than bind him.

04.n: The brief's Greek text spells the town Ἀβλαά.

07.n: τοῦ μὴ βασιλεύειν, 'so as not to reign'.

09.n: ἔδωκεν, 'he gave': the Greek has no word for the fine or for 'on the land', and reads as though the sum was simply paid.

14.n: τάλαντον, talent: the word our register renders 'talent' in the New Testament.

15.n: ἀργύριον, silver: the word our register renders 'silver' in the New Testament.
